items.title: These 4 behaviors predict divorce with startling accuracy
items.description:
Every marriage’s disintegration is marked by the same four warning signs that researchers John and Julie Gottman can spot before a couple even finishes their first sentence. 
 The founders of the Gottman Institute break down decades of lab research on why relationships collapse, and what to look for in a partner so they can make it 50 years by your side. 
 
 This video  These 4 behaviors predict divorce with startling accuracy  is featured on  Big Think .

items.description:
“Some people will hate what I say,” the mathematician Marcus du Sautoy tells me, “because it’s all about unweaving the rainbow. Some people want to retain the magic and don’t want to know why something’s working. That’s fine. items.title: What living systems teach us about true agency
items.description:
We call AI systems “agents” all the time. But what does “agency” actually mean?  
 Alan Love, philosopher and professor at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, argues that biology offers a more careful way to think about goal-directed behavior, function, and, eventually, machine intelligence. items.title: When to trust your intuition (and when not to)
items.description:
Intuition is having a moment. If you listen to podcasts or read nonfiction books, you’ll hear similar advice: trust your gut, listen to your body, follow your instincts. 
 The trouble is that what we colloquially call “intuition” carries no label telling you where it came from. It can be based on expertise built over years. But sometimes it’s a cognitive bias. And sometimes it’s just fear.

items.title: The community healthcare model transforming lives across West Africa
items.description:
In parts of West Africa, getting sick used to mean navigating a maze of barriers — distance, cost, time spent away from work — before ever seeing a health worker. Muso set out to change that. 
 Working hand-in-hand with governments, they built a model where professional community health workers bring care directly to patients’ doors within 24 hours, at no cost. items.title: 3 ways to make your own luck
items.description:
Three people are sitting on a bench: a wise man between two fools.

items.title: Gravity can’t be an instantaneous force
items.description: When you look at the Sun, the light you’re seeing isn’t the light that’s being emitted right now. Instead, you’re seeing light that’s a little more than eight minutes old, since the Sun is some 150 million kilometers (93 million miles) away, and light — although it’s fast — can only travel through the Universe at a specific speed: the speed of light.
